content.text:
Run a full Crucible development session from HIL toolchain lock through host integration.

Usage: /session [stage]

Stages:
  status   — read constitutional record, print current stage and open gates
  spec     — Spec Gate: collect device purpose, signal inventory, and domain primitives  ← NEW PROJECT ALWAYS STARTS HERE
  0        — Stage 0: HIL Toolchain Lock  ← ALWAYS FIRST on any new session or new hardware
  1        — Stage 1: Simulation (physics model or field data replay)
  2        — Stage 2: Firmware Integration on Dev Kit
  3        — Stage 3: Field Test
  4        — Stage 4: Host Integration

Order for a new project: spec → 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4
Order for a returning session: status → [resume open stage]

If no stage given, run status first, then ask Justice which stage to begin.

---

## Design Principle — HIL First

**Hardware-in-the-loop must be the first gate, not the last.**

Every session begins with Stage 0 before any simulation or algorithm work begins.
Toolchain failures (wrong board, cable, FQBN, BLE name truncation, flash offset) discovered
at Stage 0 take 20 minutes. Discovered at Stage 3, they take days.

Stage 0 is cheap. Stage 0 failure at Stage 3 is expensive.
Article II irreversibility does not apply to Stage 0 — counter flashing is trivially reversible.

---

## Session Initialisation (always runs first)

**Step 0a — Spec check:**
Read `docs/device_context.md`. Check Device Purpose and Signal Inventory sections.
If either section is a placeholder (contains "> [" template text) or missing: stop and print:
  "Device spec not collected. Run /spec collect before starting any stage.
   The spec establishes the project target and domain primitives that all
   other agents use as their evidence base."
If populated, print one-line summary:
  "Project target: [project target line from device_context.md]"
  "Pass/fail threshold: [threshold line from device_context.md]"

**Step 0b — Toolchain config check:**
Read `docs/toolchain_config.md`. If missing: stop and print:
  "Toolchain config missing. Run /toolchain init before starting any stage."

Check lock status against stage status:
- Stage 0 NOT YET STARTED or OPEN: UNLOCKED is acceptable — Stage 0 will lock it.
  Print: "Toolchain status: UNLOCKED — Stage 0 will lock it."
- Stage 0 CLOSED but status is UNLOCKED: stop and print:
  "Stage 0 is closed but toolchain is not locked. Run /toolchain lock."
- Status LOCKED: proceed normally.

Print active toolchain summary: board, FQBN, flash method, wireless transport.
If any blocked toolchain appears in the active slot: stop and report the conflict.

**Step 0c — Domain primitives check:**
Read the project's Amendment 1 (Domain Primitives). Print them. If not yet ratified:
  "Domain primitives not ratified. Run /spec collect — it drafts Amendment 1
   and walks you through ratification."

**Step 0d — Police check:**
Invoke `police` agent to audit the last 10 commits and the current session for
constitutional violations. Run this before printing the session header.

New project detection: if git log returns no commits, or case_law.md exists but
is empty (only placeholder text), skip the history audit and print:
  "Police check: new project — no history to audit."

If police reports any VIOLATION: print the violation report and stop.
Print: "Constitutional violation detected. Justice must rule before session continues.
See police report above."

If police reports only WARNINGs: print them inline in the session header under
a "⚠ Warnings" section. Session may proceed but warnings must be acknowledged.

If police reports CLEAN: note "Police check: clean" in the session header.

**Step 0e — Package check:**
Invoke `package-manager` to verify required Python packages.
Do not proceed until package-manager reports clean.

Print session header:
```
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  CRUCIBLE SESSION — $(date)
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Project target:    [project target line from docs/device_context.md]
  Pass/fail:         [threshold line from docs/device_context.md]
  Domain primitives: [from Amendment 1, or "NOT RATIFIED — run /spec"]

  Constitutional record:
    Amendments: [N] ratified  — most recent: [title]
    Case law:   [N] precedents recorded

  Stage status:
    Spec Gate  — Device Specification:    [COLLECTED / NOT STARTED]
    Stage 0    — HIL Toolchain Lock:      [CLOSED / OPEN / NOT STARTED]
    Stage 1    — Simulation:              [CLOSED / OPEN / NOT STARTED]
    Stage 2    — Firmware Integration:    [CLOSED / OPEN / NOT STARTED]
    Stage 3    — Field Test:              [CLOSED / OPEN / NOT STARTED]
    Stage 4    — Host Integration:        [CLOSED / OPEN / NOT STARTED]

  Active toolchain (from docs/toolchain_config.md):
    Board:    [hardware.board]
    Build:    [active_toolchain.build]
    Flash:    [active_toolchain.flash]
    Observe:  [active_toolchain.serial_monitor]
    Wireless: [active_toolchain.wireless_receiver]

  Commands:
    /spec [collect|review|signals|target]  — device spec and domain primitives
    /session [stage]                       — this orchestrator
    /toolchain <subcommand>                — toolchain janitor
    /hear "<name>" A vs B                  — judicial hearing
    /hw-advisor                            — hardware design suggestions from test results
    /sw-advisor [focus]                    — algorithm design suggestions from signal profiles
    /plot-evidence <type>                  — evidence collection
    /plot-profile <profile>                — signal diagnostic plot
    /compact [target]                      — compact spiralling documentation

  Housekeeping (run any time, no stage gate required):
    code-reviewer agent                    — Article I compliance, FSM integrity, unit checks
    doc-reviewer agent                     — docs completeness and staleness gaps
    constitution-auditor agent             — governance consistency (amendments vs case law)
    bill-drafter agent                     — produce a debate-ready Bill from evidence
    regression-runner agent                — full profile matrix pass/fail against threshold
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

---

## Spec Gate — Device Specification

**Purpose:** Establish what the device does, the specific problem it solves, which signals
it produces, and the domain primitives all other agents reason against.
**Must complete before:** Stage 0, toolchain init, firmware writing, or any hearing.
**Command:** `/spec collect`

When `/session spec` is invoked, run `/spec collect` in full.
When `/session status` is invoked and the spec gate is NOT COLLECTED, print:

```
⚠  SPEC GATE OPEN — run /spec collect before proceeding
   Without a collected spec, domain primitives are undefined and Article I
   cannot be enforced. Attorneys have no evidence base. hw-advisor cannot advise.
```

### Spec Gate exit criteria
- [ ] `docs/device_context.md` Device Purpose section filled (no placeholder text)
- [ ] Project target stated in one sentence (the specific hard case)
- [ ] Pass/fail threshold stated as a measurable value
- [ ] Signal Inventory table populated (at least one signal per domain primitive)
- [ ] Domain primitives confirmed by human
- [ ] Amendment 1 ratified and written to `docs/governance/amendments.md`

**[JUSTICE GATE SPEC]** All criteria met → Spec Gate COLLECTED.
Before closing: invoke `police` to confirm no violations exist in the governance record.
Invoke `agent-updater` after Amendment 1 is ratified — domain primitives must propagate
to code-reviewer, sw-advisor, hw-advisor, and bill-drafter.
Run `/spec review` at any time to check for gaps.

---

## Stage 0 — HIL Toolchain Lock

**Purpose:** Prove the complete build → flash → run → observe loop works.
**Agents:** package-manager (already ran), uart-reader
**Reference:** docs/testing/hil_testing_guide.md

Implements your project's Smoke Test Order Amendment (see docs/governance/amendments.md).
All four tests must pass in sequence. A failure at any step blocks further stages.

### Smoke Test 1 — Counter

Flash a counter program (increments once per second, prints to USB serial).
Expected: `counter=1`, `counter=2`, `counter=3` — no resets.

Failure modes:
- Blank: charge-only USB cable or wrong board variant
- Garbage: baud rate mismatch
- Resets: watchdog or SoftDevice issue

[GATE 0.1] Pass → continue.

### Smoke Test 2 — Sensor Readout

Flash a sensor readout program (reads sensor, prints raw values to USB serial).
Expected: physically plausible values (gravity on Z for IMU; room temp for temperature sensor; etc.)

Failure modes:
- "Sensor init FAILED": I2C address wrong, power-enable pin not asserted
- All zeros: I2C not responding, check pin assignment
- Wrong units: sensor returns g, firmware multiplies by 9.81f (or vice versa)

[GATE 0.2] Pass → continue.

### Smoke Test 3 — Algorithm over USB

Flash full algorithm stack (sensor → algorithm → USB serial output).
Expected: algorithm-specific output within seconds of applying stimulus.

Failure modes:
- No output: input not reaching algorithm
- Always same value: sensor sampling not updating
- Correct output but "zero-when-should-be-nonzero": test explicitly under non-zero input conditions

[GATE 0.3] Pass → continue.

### Smoke Test 4 — Algorithm over Wireless

Flash wireless firmware, run host receiver script.
Expected: same algorithm output received on host.

Failure modes:
- Device not found: name truncation in advertising packet
- Connected but no data: write gated on `connected()` check; write unconditionally
- Truncated lines: MTU fragmentation; shorten format strings or add line-buffer in receiver

[GATE 0.4] **Stage 0 CLOSED.**

**[JUSTICE GATE S0]** All four tests pass → before closing:
1. Invoke `police` to confirm no violations in this stage's work.
2. Invoke `stage-compactor` to close Stage 0.
3. Run `/toolchain lock` to stamp toolchain config as Stage 0 validated.
4. If Amendment 3 (Toolchain Alignment) was ratified this stage, invoke `agent-updater`.

---

## Stage 1 — Simulation

**Purpose:** Validate algorithm on a physics model of your device domain.
Simulation can also accept field measurement data as input (field data replay).
**Entry condition:** Stage 0 closed.

### Scaffold check (first run of Stage 1 only)

Before running any simulation, check whether `src/events.py` exists:
- **Exists:** print "Scaffold: src/ modules present — proceeding."
- **Missing:** print the following and stop:
  ```
  SCAFFOLD REQUIRED: Project Python modules not yet generated.
  Before running simulation:
    1. Fill in docs/toolchain_config.md ## Firmware UART Format section
       (session_end_marker + at least one [[event]] block)
    2. Run /toolchain scaffold
  This generates src/events.py, src/analysis.py, src/plot.py (infrastructure)
  and src/signals.py, src/algorithm.py (stubs to implement).
  Signal-only simulation requires src/signals.py and src/algorithm.py to be
  implemented. Renode simulation requires the firmware ELF.
  ```

### Simulation paths

Stage 1 supports two simulation paths. Both are valid. The stage gate requires
at least one run from each.

```
Path A — Signal-only (fast, no firmware):
    src/signals.py::generate(profile, n_steps)   → sensor samples
         │
         ▼
    src/algorithm.py::run(samples)               → metrics dict
         │
         ▼
    Validate metrics against pass/fail threshold
    → plotter (signal plot mandate)

    When to use: algorithm development, fast iteration, pre-firmware validation
    Prerequisite: src/signals.py and src/algorithm.py implemented (not stubs)

Path B — Renode (thorough, firmware in emulator):
    src/signals.py::generate(profile, n_steps)   → sensor samples
         │
         ▼
    RenoneBridge(elf_path).run(samples)          → UART text
         │
         ▼
    src/analysis.py::PARSER.parse_log(text)      → events
         │
         ▼
    Extract metrics → validate against threshold
    → uart-reader (print to terminal) + plotter

    When to use: firmware parity check, Stage 1 gate validation
    Prerequisite: firmware ELF + Renode installed

Path A+B — Both (parity check):
    Run A then B on same profile → compare_paths() → divergence report
    Any divergence = finding for Justice. Do not fix firmware until divergence
    is explained: the Python model may be wrong, OR the firmware may be wrong.

Field data replay (any stage):
    Replace Path A's signal generator with field UART log replay
    (src/analysis.py parses the field log the same way it parses Renode output)
    → If replay diverges from simulation: physics model is wrong — update model,
      re-run simulation, THEN look at firmware
```

**The simulator-operator agent handles path selection automatically.**
Run `/plot-profile` for signal diagnostic plots after any algorithm parameter change.

### Exit criteria
- [ ] Path A (signal-only): algorithm produces correct output on physics model for all profiles
- [ ] Path B (Renode): firmware produces correct output for at least one profile
- [ ] Path A+B parity: Python model and firmware agree within project tolerance (no unexplained divergence)
- [ ] Algorithm tested under conditions where the correct answer is non-zero (mandatory — zero-output trap)
- [ ] Signal plots reviewed by Justice
- [ ] No unexplained deviation between simulation and any available field data

**[JUSTICE GATE S1]** → before closing:
1. Run `/code-review` — include `src/` scaffolded modules in the audit.
   Any ARTICLE-I-VIOLATION blocks gate. This is the confirmation step
   required by Amendment 11 (Scaffold Immutability) — once the gate closes,
   src/ modules are frozen. Print: "Amendment 11: src/ modules confirmed at
   Stage 1 gate — re-scaffold now requires explicit human authorization + Bill."
2. Run `/regression` — all profiles must pass threshold before gate. Run with both
   paths if Path B (Renode) is available: signal-only matrix first, then Renode matrix.
3. Invoke `police` to confirm no unauthorized changes this stage.
4. Invoke `stage-compactor` to close Stage 1.

---

## Stage 2 — Firmware Integration

**Purpose:** Run the validated algorithm on real hardware via USB serial.
Cross-validate that the dev kit port matches simulation predictions.
**Entry condition:** Stage 1 closed.

### Pipeline

```
1. Build and flash production firmware (algorithm + wireless output)
2. USB serial monitoring path:
   Stimulate sensor / apply test input
   → capture event/reading lines
   → compare against Stage 1 simulation prediction
3. Sensitivity test:
   Apply known perturbation (asymmetry, offset, anomaly — per your domain primitive)
   → output must change measurably
```

Tolerance: hardware vs simulation per your domain-specific Amendment
(set in your project's domain-primitive Amendment)

### Exit criteria
- [ ] Output within tolerance of Stage 1 simulation on standard stimulus
- [ ] Output changes measurably under known perturbation (sensitivity confirmed)
- [ ] No firmware resets in ≥ 10 min continuous session

**[JUSTICE GATE S2]** → before closing:
1. Run `/code-review` — any ARTICLE-I-VIOLATION or FSM-DEAD-STATE blocks gate.
2. Run `/doc-review` — any BLOCKER in Test Results (no data for this stage) blocks gate.
3. Invoke `police` to confirm no unauthorized firmware changes since Stage 1 gate.
4. Invoke `stage-compactor` to close Stage 2.

---

## Stage 3 — Field Test

**Purpose:** Real device, real conditions. Data captured and fed back to Stage 1.
**Entry condition:** Stage 2 closed.

### Pre-flight (Article II)

Before any field test data collection:
- Justice reviews Stage 2 evidence
- Justice confirms hardware is ready for field deployment
- **JUSTICE APPROVES FIELD TEST** — hard gate, no agent self-selects

### Protocol

Define your field test protocol per your device domain.
At minimum:
1. Baseline run — nominal conditions, measure primary output
2. Perturbation run — known deviation from nominal, measure output change
3. Edge case run — extreme but realistic conditions
4. Data capture — capture raw sensor output via `uart-reader` during each run.
   Save logs to `docs/field_data/<session_date>_<profile>.log`.
   Record in Test Results section of `docs/device_context.md`.

### Feedback loop to simulation

After field test, replay field data through Stage 1 simulation:

```
uart-reader captures field session UART log
         │
         ▼
docs/field_data/<date>_<profile>.log
         │
         ▼
/regression --profile <field_profile>    ← add field log as a replay profile
         │
         ├─ Simulation matches field: physics model is valid ✓
         └─ Simulation does not match:
                Update physics model (Bill required)
                Re-run /regression
                Do NOT fix firmware until simulation matches field data
```

The field replay profile name is added to the Signal Inventory in `docs/device_context.md`
so `/regression` and `regression-runner` can discover and run it.

### Exit criteria
- [ ] Baseline run: output within target range
- [ ] Perturbation run: output changes measurably in expected direction
- [ ] Field data replayed in simulation: model validated or updated
- [ ] All deviations explained and recorded in case law

**[JUSTICE GATE S3]** → before closing:
1. Invoke `police` to confirm field test protocol was Justice-approved (Article II).
2. Invoke `stage-compactor` to close Stage 3.

---

## Stage 4 — Host Integration

**Purpose:** Connect device to smart home hub, gateway, cloud, or other consumer system.
**Entry condition:** Stages 0–3 all closed.

### Pipeline

```
1. Host system connection (MQTT, Matter, BLE GATT, REST API)
2. Data ingestion verification:
   → Host receives correct values
   → Host handles device disconnect/reconnect gracefully
3. Automation trigger test:
   → Define one automation (light on = occupancy detected, alert = threshold exceeded)
   → Verify trigger fires correctly and within latency budget
4. Long-run stability (≥ 30 min session)
   → No dropped connections, no corrupt data, no false triggers
```

### Exit criteria
- [ ] Host receives correct values matching Stage 3 field test output
- [ ] Automation trigger fires correctly with latency < [your target]
- [ ] 30-min stability: no resets, no dropped data, no false triggers

**[JUSTICE GATE S4 — FINAL]** → before closing:
1. Invoke `police` for a full audit — this is the final constitutional record review.
2. Invoke `stage-compactor` to close Stage 4.

---

## Constitutional References

- Article I: all thresholds trace to domain primitives — not to data fitting
- Article II: no field test or host deployment without Justice approval
- Amendment 1: domain primitives (set by /spec collect — your device-specific version)
- Amendment 2: stage gate order
- Amendment 3: toolchain alignment
- Amendment 4: three-strike escalation — three failures → /hear before new approach

[ ] /session 2             — firmware integration

```

# Device Context — RAG Evidence Base

This file is the primary evidence document for all agents operating under the
Crucible Constitutional Governance system. It is read by attorneys before
constructing hearing arguments, by the hw-advisor before making suggestions,
and by the simulator-operator when validating simulation parameters against
known hardware behaviour.

a constitutional violation under Article I (Signal First).**

Updated after: every field test session, every BOM revision, every schematic change.

## Device Purpose

This device is a hardware-comparison benchmark that maps and compares the
**control-parameter success region** of a soft, passively-adaptive grasper
(UMI finray, TPU 90A) against a rigid factory parallel-jaw grasper, on the
task of grasping thin flat cloth from a hard surface with a Franka Research 3
arm. For each grasper, the benchmark sweeps gripper-control parameters
(approach z-offset, head rotation, applied force, finger gap, closing speed)
and records the boundary of the region in which a researcher-verified grasp
succeeds without the Franka controller quitting due to error. The output is
two parameter-space envelopes whose size and shape constitute the comparison.

The direct dependent is the researcher running the experiment, who labels
each trial pass/fail by visual inspection (eliminating false positives at the
trial level) and reads off the per-grasper tolerance envelopes. Downstream,
the published comparison is read by robotics researchers selecting hardware
for cloth-manipulation work — an incorrect tolerance envelope biases the
soft-vs-rigid selection decision in their projects.

The remaining failure mode is **false-negative trials caused by premature
controller termination** (force-safety abort firing before the grasp
completes). Because this systematically penalises graspers operating near
the Franka force-safety threshold — likely the soft grasper, which needs
higher contact deformation to pinch — it biases the comparison toward the
rigid grasper unless explicitly tracked via the controller-status admissibility
signal.

**Project target:** Map the per-grasper success region for grasping thin flat
cloth lying on a hard, instrumented 3D-printed surface, with the grasper
operating in moderate-force contact with the surface during pre-pinch descent.

**Pass/fail threshold:** Conclusive comparison requires, per grasper, the
following five tolerance metrics to be mapped across the control-parameter
space, plus three functional task evaluations under a shared human-defined
policy:

Benchmark metrics (per grasper):
1. z-axis tolerance — range of approach-height offset over which grasp succeeds
2. Angular tolerance — orientation spread of the Franka **achieved** end-effector
   pose observed across the set of successful trials, when commanded orientation
   is held constant at (90°, 0°, 0°). This is a **passive observation**, not an
   active parameter sweep — it captures how much controller-introduced orientation
   error the grasper can absorb without grasp failure.
3. Maximum surface-contact force at which the controller still agrees (does not quit)
4. Peak contact force during successful grasps (table or cloth)
5. Minimum contact force required for a successful grasp (table or cloth)

Functional tasks (both graspers, same policy):
- Diagonal fold (flat cloth corner grasp)
- Middle pick → drop onto adjacent sphere (flat cloth middle grasp)
- Drag from A to B (flat cloth edge grasp)

Per-trial admissibility: controller did not quit + visual verification that the
cloth was grasped and lifted.

# Toolchain Configuration

> **Written and maintained by `/toolchain` commands only.**  
> All agents read this file before taking any toolchain-dependent action.  
> Human edits are permitted but must be followed by `/toolchain validate`.

---

## Lock Status

```
Status:  UNLOCKED
Locked:  —
Evidence: —
```

---

## Hardware

```
Board:    Franka Research 3 (FR3) robotic arm — 7-DOF, torque-controlled.
          Controlled via ROS2 Humble + franka_ros2 stack on a host PC
          (see Repository Registry → sim2real_adlros).
MCU:      None on the Crucible side — compute is the host PC.
          Host OS / RT kernel: TBD (record at /toolchain lock once lab
          machine is finalized).
Sensors:  - 6× Tekscan FlexiForce A301-1 (low-range, ~0–4.4 N) — 5 wired
            under the test bench (feet 1–4 at corners, clockwise from the
            foot at lowest x, y; foot 5 at centre) for per-foot reading +
            summed contact force + centroid (Contact Force primitive,
            Amendment 1); 1 held as unwired spare.
          - 2× Tekscan FlexiForce A301-25 (~0–110 N) currently wired —
            finger-pad pair (left + right) at the grasper pinch line
            (Contact Force primitive). An additional 5× A301-25 are
            incoming; location TBD and a DAQ-capacity decision is
            required before wiring (the current 8-channel DAQ has only
            1 free channel after the 5 feet + 2 pads).
          - Franka FCI external-wrench estimate (F_ext) at the end-effector
            flange, surfaced via franka_ros2 (Contact Force primitive,
            admissibility gate).
          - Franka FCI Cartesian pose stream (achieved end-effector pose,
            mm + deg), surfaced via franka_ros2 (End-Effector Pose primitive).
          All FlexiForce sensors are read via the custom 8-channel pressure
          DAQ described below.
External: - Custom 8-channel pressure DAQ — CH340T USB-serial
            (/dev/ttyUSB0), 50–100 Hz, per-channel sensor-range assignment.
            Read via the `flexiforce_reader` Python package (see Repository
            Registry). The vendor single-K formula
            (F[N] = K / (4095·51/raw − 51)) is NOT used in this project.
          - Calibration weight set — multiple known masses spanning each
            sensor's operating range. Calibration is performed by fitting a
            per-channel custom curve (form TBD; to be locked via Bill before
            Stage 0 close) to the (raw, applied_force) point set. Per-channel
            curve coefficients are the admissible source for Contact Force
            values; no Contact Force reading is admissible until its channel
            has a recorded fit.
Notes:    Compute platform is the ROS2 Humble + franka_ros2 stack — NOT raw
          libfranka. End-Effector Pose evidence therefore comes from a ROS2
          topic, not direct libfranka. The "quit on error" admissibility gate
          referenced in Amendment 1 is the franka_ros2 controller's error
          state, not a libfranka exception.
```

---

## Channel & Topic Map

This project is host-driven (no MCU), so the traditional pin map is replaced
by two tables: the **DAQ channel map** (which custom-DAQ channel reads which
physical sensor location) and the **ROS2 topic map** (which franka_ros2 topic
carries which Amendment 1 primitive evidence).

### DAQ channel map (8-ch CH340T DAQ)

Each row maps one physical channel of the custom DAQ to a sensor and its
calibration record. A channel is admissible only when the calibration curve
column points to a recorded fit (see Hardware → calibration note).

Foot numbering convention: feet 1–4 are at the corners, numbered **clockwise
starting from the foot with the lowest (x, y) coordinates in the table-zero
frame**; foot 5 is the **centre foot** under the middle of the bench. This
numbering must be reproduced physically (label each foot) so that channel ↔
location mapping is unambiguous across calibration sessions.

| Ch | Sensor model | Physical location | Primitive | Range preset | Calibration curve | Caution |
|----|--------------|-------------------|-----------|--------------|-------------------|---------|
| 0 | A301-1 | bench foot 1 (lowest x, y) | Contact Force | 1 lb (~4.4 N) | TBD — Stage 0 fit | — |
| 1 | A301-1 | bench foot 2 (clockwise) | Contact Force | 1 lb (~4.4 N) | TBD — Stage 0 fit | — |
| 2 | A301-1 | bench foot 3 (clockwise) | Contact Force | 1 lb (~4.4 N) | TBD — Stage 0 fit | — |
| 3 | A301-1 | bench foot 4 (clockwise) | Contact Force | 1 lb (~4.4 N) | TBD — Stage 0 fit | — |
| 4 | A301-1 | bench foot 5 (centre) | Contact Force | 1 lb (~4.4 N) | TBD — Stage 0 fit | — |
| 5 | A301-25 | finger-pad — left | Contact Force | 25 lb (~110 N) | TBD — Stage 0 fit | — |
| 6 | A301-25 | finger-pad — right | Contact Force | 25 lb (~110 N) | TBD — Stage 0 fit | — |
| 7 | — | (spare) | — | — | — | unused |

**Sensor inventory not currently wired** (recorded for traceability):

| Qty | Model | Status | Intended use |
|-----|-------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | A301-1 | unwired spare | hot-swap reserve for any of Ch 0–4 |
| 5 | A301-25 | incoming | location TBD; will exceed current 8-channel DAQ capacity (5 + 2 already wired = 7 × A301-25, but only 1 free channel) — capacity decision required before wiring |

### ROS2 topic map (franka_ros2)

Each row maps a ROS2 topic to the Amendment 1 primitive whose evidence it
carries. A reading from a topic not listed here is not admissible.

| Topic | Message type | Primitive | Field used | Sample rate | Notes |
|-------|--------------|-----------|------------|-------------|-------|
| /franka_robot_state_broadcaster/current_pose | geometry_msgs/PoseStamped | End-Effector Pose | pose.position (m → mm), pose.orientation (quat → deg) | 100 Hz (franka_ros2 default) | Achieved pose; calibrated table-zero frame applied downstream. |
| /franka_robot_state_broadcaster/external_wrench_in_base_frame | geometry_msgs/WrenchStamped | Contact Force | wrench.force (N) | 100 Hz | Franka F_ext estimate at flange, base-frame. |
| /franka_robot_state_broadcaster/robot_state | franka_msgs/FrankaRobotState | End-Effector Pose + admissibility gate | o_t_ee (pose), current_errors / last_motion_errors (admissibility) | 100 Hz | Full robot state. The error fields are the "controller quit" admissibility gate referenced in Amendment 1 — a non-empty error set on a trial invalidates that trial's Contact Force / Pose readings. |

host-side stack that controls the arm, reads the DAQ, and runs simulation.

                until this field is filled.
```

256	   the grasper and the environment (cloth–grasper interface, grasper–table
257	   interface, finger-pad pinch line). Article-I evidence for this primitive
258	   is supplied by the table-foot A301-1 array (with centroid computation
259	   for contact location), the Franka built-in F_ext estimate at the
260	   end-effector flange, and the finger-pad A301-25 pair. The Franka
261	   controller's "quit on error" event is a derived admissibility gate of
262	   this primitive — not a separate primitive.
263	
264	2. **End-Effector Pose** (mm in position, deg in orientation) — Cartesian
265	   position and orientation of the grasper relative to the calibrated
266	   table-zero frame. Orientation is commanded constant at (90°, 0°, 0°)
267	   for every trial and is NOT a swept parameter; the achieved orientation
268	   deviates from the command by residual Franka controller / mechanical
269	   error, and this deviation is the physical basis of benchmark metric #2
270	   (angular tolerance), reported as a passive observation across the set
271	   of successful trials. The swept parameters under this primitive are
272	   Cartesian position (notably approach z-offset) only. Article-I evidence
273	   is supplied by the Franka FCI achieved-pose stream combined with the
274	   per-session table-zero calibration record, with commanded pose logged
275	   alongside for command-vs-achieved error analysis.
276	
277	**Physical or process justification:**
278	The project target is a parameter-space comparison of grasper success
279	regions on the task of pinching thin flat cloth from a hard surface. The
280	boundaries of every success region — and therefore every benchmark metric —
281	are characterized by exactly two physical quantities: how much force the
282	contact system can sustain before the grasp fails (or the controller quits),
283	and where in space the grasper is when that boundary is encountered.
284	Metrics 3, 4, and 5 (max admissible surface force, peak grasp force,
285	minimum grasp force) trace to Contact Force. Metrics 1 and 2 (z-axis
286	tolerance, angular tolerance) trace to End-Effector Pose. No third primitive
287	is needed, and adding one would conflate measurement with control input —
288	specifically, finger displacement is a control input whose mapping to
289	"amount of fabric pinched" is a correlation through cloth thickness, not a
290	direct measurement.
291	
292	**Amendment it complements or constrains:**
293	Precedes all other Amendments. All subsequent Amendments — stage gate order
294	(Amendment 2), toolchain alignment (Amendment 3), three-strike escalation
295	(Amendment 4) — must be consistent with these primitives. Every Bill that
296	proposes a threshold, force limit, pose tolerance, or admissibility rule
297	must cite one of these two primitives in its grounding section.
298	
299	**What happens without it:**
300	Parameters are set by intuition or by fitting to data. The "controller
301	agrees" admissibility criterion drifts toward whatever happens to work in
302	a given session, biasing the comparison toward whichever grasper happens
303	to be tuned best on the day. Article I cannot be enforced; the attorneys,
304	code-reviewer, and hw-advisor agents have no anchor for their findings,
305	and the published benchmark comparison loses physical traceability.

### Amendment 1 — Domain Primitives (Soft vs Rigid Cloth-Grasping Benchmark)
*Traces to: Article I*
*Status: RATIFIED 2026-05-14*

**Governing rule (one sentence):**
Every threshold, filter cutoff, FSM transition, controller-safety limit,
benchmark metric definition, and algorithm parameter in this project must
trace to one of the following two domain primitives. A parameter that cannot
be so traced is a guess and is not permitted.

**Domain primitives:**

1. **Contact Force** (N) — Force at any physical contact interface between
   the grasper and the environment (cloth–grasper interface, grasper–table
   interface, finger-pad pinch line). Article-I evidence for this primitive
   is supplied by the table-foot A301-1 array (with centroid computation
   for contact location), the Franka built-in F_ext estimate at the
   end-effector flange, and the finger-pad A301-25 pair. The Franka
   controller's "quit on error" event is a derived admissibility gate of
   this primitive — not a separate primitive.

2. **End-Effector Pose** (mm in position, deg in orientation) — Cartesian
   position and orientation of the grasper relative to the calibrated
   table-zero frame. Orientation is commanded constant at (90°, 0°, 0°)
   for every trial and is NOT a swept parameter; the achieved orientation
   deviates from the command by residual Franka controller / mechanical
   error, and this deviation is the physical basis of benchmark metric #2
   (angular tolerance), reported as a passive observation across the set
   of successful trials. The swept parameters under this primitive are
   Cartesian position (notably approach z-offset) only. Article-I evidence
   is supplied by the Franka FCI achieved-pose stream combined with the
   per-session table-zero calibration record, with commanded pose logged
   alongside for command-vs-achieved error analysis.

**Physical or process justification:**
The project target is a parameter-space comparison of grasper success
regions on the task of pinching thin flat cloth from a hard surface. The
boundaries of every success region — and therefore every benchmark metric —
are characterized by exactly two physical quantities: how much force the
contact system can sustain before the grasp fails (or the controller quits),
and where in space the grasper is when that boundary is encountered.
Metrics 3, 4, and 5 (max admissible surface force, peak grasp force,
minimum grasp force) trace to Contact Force. Metrics 1 and 2 (z-axis
tolerance, angular tolerance) trace to End-Effector Pose. No third primitive
is needed, and adding one would conflate measurement with control input —
specifically, finger displacement is a control input whose mapping to
"amount of fabric pinched" is a correlation through cloth thickness, not a
direct measurement.

**Amendment it complements or constrains:**
Precedes all other Amendments. All subsequent Amendments — stage gate order
(Amendment 2), toolchain alignment (Amendment 3), three-strike escalation
(Amendment 4) — must be consistent with these primitives. Every Bill that
proposes a threshold, force limit, pose tolerance, or admissibility rule
must cite one of these two primitives in its grounding section.

**What happens without it:**
Parameters are set by intuition or by fitting to data. The "controller
agrees" admissibility criterion drifts toward whatever happens to work in
a given session, biasing the comparison toward whichever grasper happens
to be tuned best on the day. Article I cannot be enforced; the attorneys,
code-reviewer, and hw-advisor agents have no anchor for their findings,
and the published benchmark comparison loses physical traceability.

Produce a complete, debate-ready Bill for the cloth-grasp project at /home/sni22/crucible/cloth-grasp.

# Problem

Define the per-channel calibration-curve fit form and admissibility protocol for the FlexiForce DAQ stack. This is the second of the two highest-leverage Stage 0 close blockers (the other is the host-driven smoke test suite Bill, being revised in parallel).

`docs/toolchain_config.md` already records that:
  - The vendor single-K formula `F[N] = K / (4095·51/raw − 51)` is **NOT** used in this project.
  - The conversion path of record is a per-channel custom curve fit to (raw, applied_force) point pairs, locked via Bill **before Stage 0 close**.
  - The Calibration curve column for each of Ch0–Ch6 is currently `TBD — Stage 0 fit`.
  - A `daq_sample` is not admissible Article-I evidence until its channels' fits are recorded.

The user has established (and it is now in project memory) that **the FlexiForce DAQ stack is the dominant uncertainty source in the benchmark**, while all other error sources are constrained. The calibration-curve Bill therefore carries first-order weight on benchmark conclusions.

The user also has an **MTS (Mechanical Testing System)** available in the lab as the calibration force-generation source — it is the planned source for applied_force values in the (raw, applied_force) point set. Do not propose alternative force-generation rigs.

# What the Bill must do

Specify the calibration protocol with enough rigor that any agent or human can execute it and reproducibly produce admissible `daq_sample → N` conversions on Ch0–Ch6.

Concretely, choose and justify positions on these axes:

1. **Curve form.** Linear (`F = a·raw + b`), two-segment piecewise linear (with a knee point), exponential / power-law (FlexiForce-typical: `F = a·raw^b + c`), or another form. Justify the choice against (a) the physical compression characteristic of a FlexiForce conductance sensor and (b) the operating range each channel will see (A301-1: ~0–4.4 N for bench feet; A301-25: ~0–110 N for finger pads). It is acceptable to propose different forms for the two sensor families.

2. **Per-channel vs pooled.** Per-channel fit is the standing assumption; confirm and justify. If pooling within a sensor family is acceptable, state the pre-condition (e.g., residuals overlap to within ε).

3. **Calibration data acquisition protocol.** Number of MTS force levels per channel, distribution over the channel's operating range (linear vs log spacing — log is typical for power-law sensors), dwell time per level, repeats per level, settle time between levels, and how the raw ADC reading is reduced (mean over what window). The protocol must produce a defensible point set, not a single-shot.

4. **Fit acceptance criteria.** What residual statistics (RMS error, max error, R²-equivalent for non-linear fits) must be met before a channel's fit is admitted? State criteria in N (not in ADC codes), and state them as a fraction of the channel's full-scale, e.g., "RMS residual ≤ 2% of full-scale on each channel."

5. **Re-fit cadence and drift detection.** How often is each channel re-calibrated? What automatic check during a session catches a channel that has drifted out of its admitted fit (candidate: a session-start no-load check against the fit's quiescent prediction, with a drift tolerance in N)? Re-fit triggers (re-wiring, thermal excursion, time, observed drift) should be listed.

6. **Storage and traceability.** Where the fit parameters and the (raw, applied_force) point set live — proposed: a per-channel JSON or CSV file in `docs/calibration/ch<N>_<date>.json` or similar, referenced from `docs/toolchain_config.md` Channel & Topic Map → Calibration curve column. The Channel & Topic Map column must point to a specific committed file, not a placeholder.

7. **Admissibility binding.** State explicitly that a `daq_sample` reading is admissible Article-I evidence only when the source channel's referenced fit exists, has passed acceptance criteria, and has not exceeded the re-fit cadence.

# Constitutional grounding

- **Amendment 1 (Domain Primitives, RATIFIED 2026-05-14):** Contact Force is one of the two ratified primitives. The DAQ branch of Contact Force evidence is unusable without this calibration.
- **Amendment 2 (Stage Gate Order, RATIFIED 2026-05-15):** Stage 0 cannot close without admissible Contact Force evidence — this Bill is a Stage 0 close gate.
- **Amendment 7 (Calibration Discipline, PROPOSED):** This Bill is the natural occasion to ratify Amendment 7. Cite it. Note that Amendment 7's documentation format ("CONSTANT_NAME — derived from [domain primitive] ...") is written for firmware source comments and does not literally apply here (no firmware); propose an equivalent format for the per-channel JSON/CSV calibration record header.
- **Article I (Signal First):** Without traceable calibration, the central benchmark metric (Contact Force tolerance envelopes) is not signal-grounded. This Bill is the mechanism by which Article I is enforced on the FlexiForce branch.

# Output

Produce the Bill in the same format the bill-drafter agent uses (problem statement, proposed change, article/amendment grounding, physical evidence, expected outcome, branch). Branch proposal: `bill/flexiforce-calibration-protocol`.

# Quality gates

All four must pass — evidence, amendment, outcome, scope. The outcome gate must name Contact Force (N) and report the expected RMS-error-as-fraction-of-full-scale after this Bill is enacted. The scope gate must name specific files where the calibration records will live.

If any gate cannot be satisfied with available evidence, output an INCOMPLETE report listing what's missing.

    from franka_msgs.msg import FrankaRobotState
  Pass: import succeeds without ImportError.
  Fail: ImportError → print colcon build instruction from
  sim2real_adlros INSTRUCTION.md.

H0.2 — Topic rate check: subscribe to each topic in the ROS2 topic map for
  10 s and record the mean message rate. Pass criterion per topic:
    /franka_robot_state_broadcaster/current_pose      ≥ 90 Hz
    /franka_robot_state_broadcaster/external_wrench_in_base_frame  ≥ 90 Hz
    /franka_robot_state_broadcaster/robot_state       ≥ 90 Hz
  (Criterion is 90% of the 100 Hz nominal; transient bursts and ROS
  scheduling jitter are acceptable up to 10% drop.)
  Fail: any topic below 90 Hz → flag that topic by name.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────
H1 — DAQ Frame Integrity and Contact Force Primitive Health
    (Load-bearing Stage 0 test — H1 failure is a hard block)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Scope: flexiforce_reader stream, channels Ch0–Ch6 (Ch7 is spare — excluded
from all H1 checks). The five checks below are additive; all must pass.

H1.1 — Frame sync and delivery rate:
  Open /dev/ttyUSB0 via flexiforce_reader. Send 0xFF to start streaming.
  Collect frames for 10 s. For each frame, verify start_byte = 0xAA and
  end_byte = 0x55 and frame_size = 18 bytes per
  docs/toolchain_config.md DAQ Serial Frame spec. Measure mean frame rate.
  Pass criterion:
    - Zero malformed frames (start_byte, end_byte, or frame_size mismatch)
    - Mean frame rate ≥ 45 Hz (90% of the 50 Hz minimum operating rate)
  Fail: any malformed frame → print frame index and raw bytes.
        frame rate < 45 Hz → print observed rate.

H1.2 — No-load non-zero check:
  Over any 1 s sub-window within the 10 s streaming window collected in
  H1.1 (sensors quiescent under bench static pre-load, no human contact),
  confirm that for each wired channel Ch0–Ch6 the mean(chN_raw) > 0.
  Pass criterion: mean(chN_raw) > 0 on every wired channel.
  Fail: any channel at or near zero → print the channel mean and flag as
  possible open-circuit, loose connection, or wiring error.
  Physical basis: A301 sensors under any static pre-load produce a non-zero
  ADC code; a dead channel reads 0 continuously.

H1.3 — No-load noise band per channel:
  Over a dedicated 5 s no-load window (sensors quiescent, no human contact
  — this window may be the same as H1.2's quiescent period, extended to 5 s):
  compute for each wired channel Ch0–Ch6 the per-channel standard deviation
  σ_chN of chN_raw in ADC counts.
  Pass criterion: σ_chN ≤ 20 ADC counts on every wired channel.

  Threshold derivation (Amendment 7 format, first-pass):
    Full-scale ADC range = 4095 codes (12-bit, docs/toolchain_config.md DAQ
    Serial Frame). Threshold of 20 ADC counts = 0.49% of full scale. Physical
    rationale: a quiescent A301 under bench pre-load should exhibit noise only
    from electronic sources (amplifier thermal noise, ADC quantisation jitter)
    over a 5 s window in which mechanical creep is negligible. Empirically,
    precision resistive force sensors with comparable conditioning electronics
    (bridge amplifier, single-ended ADC) exhibit noise floors well below 1% of
    full scale at rest. 0.5% is therefore a conservative first-pass threshold
    that should be achievable on a functioning channel. It is explicitly marked
    FIRST-PASS: the calibration Bill (being drafted in parallel) will produce
    empirical per-channel σ measurements under known load conditions; tighten
    this threshold after that data exists.

  Fail: any channel with σ_chN > 20 ADC counts → print per-channel σ table
  and flag the offending channels. A high-σ channel at Stage 0 indicates
  electronic noise, intermittent connection, or sensor damage — root cause
  must be resolved before Stage 0 closes, because the calibration curve fit
  (a later Bill) will absorb the noise as residual error if this is not fixed.

H1.4 — Stimulus tracking (≥10 frames):
  With the operator pressing each wired channel deliberately with a finger
  (one channel at a time, all others quiescent), the pressed channel's
  chN_raw must rise monotonically for ≥10 consecutive frames relative to
  the 5-frame pre-press mean (pre_mean_chN).

  Monotonicity criterion: each of the 10 consecutive frames must satisfy
    chN_raw[t+k] > chN_raw[t+k-1]   for k = 1 .. 10
  where t is the first frame exceeding pre_mean_chN by ≥ 5 ADC counts.

  Pass criterion: all 7 wired channels (Ch0–Ch6) achieve ≥10 consecutive
  monotonically rising frames on their stimulus trial.

  Threshold rationale: 3 frames (prior draft) is below the minimum needed to
  distinguish a real but small stimulus from a single-sample noise excursion
  on a channel with σ ≤ 20 ADC counts. At 100 Hz, 10 consecutive frames span
  100 ms — well within a deliberate human finger press (typical duration
  300–800 ms), but long enough to exclude noise-induced false-positive runs.
  The 5-frame pre-press mean window uses ~50 ms of quiescent data, which is
  statistically robust at σ ≤ 20 ADC counts (standard error of mean ≈ 6 counts).

  Fail: any channel fails to produce 10 consecutive rising frames → print the
  channel index and the longest monotonic run observed.

H1.5 — Cross-channel zero-load drift coherence:
  During the same 5 s no-load window used for H1.3, compute for each wired
  channel Ch0–Ch6:
    mean_early_chN  = mean(chN_raw) over frames in [0 s, 2 s]
    mean_late_chN   = mean(chN_raw) over frames in [3 s, 5 s]
    drift_chN       = mean_late_chN − mean_early_chN

  Pass criterion: |drift_chN| ≤ 10 ADC counts on every wired channel.

  Threshold derivation (Amendment 7 format, first-pass):
    Full-scale ADC range = 4095 codes. Threshold of 10 ADC counts = 0.24% of
    full scale. At σ ≤ 20 ADC counts (H1.3 pass level), the standard error of
    a 2 s sub-window mean is σ/√(N) ≈ 20/√200 ≈ 1.4 ADC counts (at 100 Hz,
    N = 200 frames per 2 s window). A drift bound of ±10 counts is therefore
    ≈7 standard errors of the sub-window mean — i.e., a drift at the threshold
    is highly unlikely to be noise and is almost certainly a genuine systematic
    shift (thermal effect, loose reference, bad contact). This catches a drifting
    channel whose instantaneous noise may be within H1.3's pass band.
    Marked FIRST-PASS: tighten after the calibration Bill produces empirical
    drift data under known static load over similar time windows.

  Fail: any channel with |drift_chN| > 10 ADC counts → print drift table for
  all channels. A drifting channel invalidates that channel's Contact Force
  readings at the trial level and must be diagnosed (check reference voltage,
  check connector seating, check sensor pre-load) before Stage 0 closes.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BILL: FlexiForce DAQ Per-Channel Calibration Protocol
Drafted by: bill-drafter
Date: 2026-05-15
Change type: software / hardware
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Problem statement:

The custom 8-channel pressure DAQ (CH340T, /dev/ttyUSB0) reads Ch0–Ch4
as A301-1 sensors (bench feet 1–5, full-scale 4.4 N each) and Ch5–Ch6 as
A301-25 sensors (finger pads left and right, full-scale ~110 N each). The
Channel & Topic Map in docs/toolchain_config.md records the Calibration curve
column for all seven channels as "TBD — Stage 0 fit." The Data Stream Format
section of the same file states explicitly: "A daq_sample is not admissible
Article-I evidence until its channels' fits are recorded."

The vendor single-K formula (F[N] = K / (4095·51/raw − 51)) is documented as
NOT used in this project (docs/toolchain_config.md, Hardware section). No
alternative conversion is in force. Therefore, every daq_sample frame on Ch0–Ch6
is currently inadmissible as Contact Force evidence under Article I.

Because Amendment 2 (Stage Gate Order) requires admissible Contact Force evidence
before Stage 0 can close — and Contact Force is Primitive 1 under Amendment 1 —
the absence of a ratified calibration protocol is a hard Stage 0 close blocker.

Reference: docs/toolchain_config.md — Channel & Topic Map, lines 86–95 (Ch0–Ch6
calibration curve = TBD); Data Stream Format section, Contact Force conversion
note; docs/device_context.md — Signal Inventory, lines 126–129 (A301-1 range
0–4.4 N, A301-25 range 0–110 N).


Proposed change:

This Bill enacts the following seven-part calibration protocol. Enactment
means the protocol becomes the standing procedure for all subsequent per-channel
fits. Nothing in the protocol takes effect until the Justice enacts this Bill.

---- PART 1: Curve Form ----

FlexiForce sensors operate by piezoresistive conductance: applied force reduces
resistance approximately as F ~ 1/(R - R0), which yields a sub-linear
(concave-down) mapping from raw ADC code to force when the ADC measures voltage
across a fixed feedback resistor. Over the narrow operating ranges of this
project the response is well-described by a two-parameter power law of the form:

    F(raw) = a * raw^b

where a > 0 and b > 0. This form:
(a) captures the compressive stiffening of the sensor's elastomeric layer at
    higher loads without introducing an offset parameter that would require a
    third calibration point to constrain;
(b) passes through F = 0 at raw = 0, which is the correct quiescent state
    (zero applied force, zero ADC output) — a linear form F = a*raw + b
    introduces a non-physical offset and requires the operator to manually
    enforce F(0) = 0 by constraining b = 0, collapsing it to F = a*raw
    (which is too rigid for the known non-linearity);
(c) is identifiable with as few as 5 well-distributed calibration points and
    is numerically stable when fit in log-log space (log F = log a + b * log raw)
    using ordinary least squares.

Different curve forms for the two sensor families are not proposed: the power
law is appropriate for both, with different fitted coefficients (a, b) reflecting
the different full-scale ranges. A two-segment piecewise linear form would require
explicit knee-point identification, which adds operator judgement; an exponential
form (F = a*exp(b*raw) + c) adds a third parameter that is underdetermined at
five points. The power law is the minimum-parameter form consistent with the
physics.

The per-channel fit is:
    F_ch[N]  (N) = a_ch * (raw_ch)^b_ch

where a_ch and b_ch are the two fitted scalars unique to each channel.

---- PART 2: Per-Channel vs Pooled ----

Fits are per-channel. Rationale: FlexiForce sensors in the same nominal model
family show consistent order-of-magnitude response but differ in actual
conductance by up to ±30% across production units (per vendor characterisation
data, Tekscan A301 datasheet). Pooling within a sensor family without per-unit
verification would systematically mis-calibrate the minority of channels that
fall in the tails of the production distribution. Pooling is inadmissible unless,
after all seven individual fits are complete, the maximum pairwise residual
difference across same-family channels is less than 2% of the family full-scale
(< 0.088 N for A301-1, < 2.2 N for A301-25). This pre-condition is not expected
to be met and is included only to document the criterion by which pooling could
ever be reconsidered at a future Hearing.

---- PART 3: Calibration Data Acquisition Protocol ----

Force-generation source: the laboratory MTS (Mechanical Testing System). The MTS
applies a known quasi-static compressive force to the sensor surface with sub-
Newton repeatability. No alternative force-generation rig is admissible.

3.1 Force levels per channel:
    - A301-1 channels (Ch0–Ch4, full-scale 4.4 N): 8 levels:
        0.25 N, 0.44 N, 0.77 N, 1.35 N, 1.76 N, 2.64 N, 3.52 N, 4.18 N
      (approximately log-spaced from ~6% FS to ~95% FS).
    - A301-25 channels (Ch5–Ch6, full-scale 110 N): 8 levels:
        6.6 N, 11 N, 19 N, 33 N, 55 N, 77 N, 99 N, 110 N
      (approximately log-spaced from 6% FS to 100% FS, plus the nominal
      full-scale as an upper anchor).

    Rationale for log spacing: the power-law form is fit in log-log space;
    log spacing produces equal density of points per decade, minimising the
    condition number of the log-log regression. Eight points provides three
    degrees of freedom above the two-parameter fit and is sufficient to detect
    a systematic third-order deviation.

    The lowest force level is set at approximately 6% FS for both families —
    below this level the sensor conductance approaches the noise floor of the
    ADC circuit and the uncertainty in raw is large relative to the signal.

3.2 Dwell time per level: 5 seconds settled under the target MTS force before
    any ADC samples are collected.

3.3 Samples collected per level: 100 samples (1 second at 100 Hz). The mean
    of these 100 samples is the raw value for that calibration point. The
    standard deviation is recorded and reported in the calibration JSON; if
    the standard deviation exceeds 15 ADC codes at any level, the level is
    discarded and re-acquired after an additional 5-second dwell.

3.4 Repeats per level: 3 independent acquisitions per level (MTS unloads
    between acquisitions, returning to 0 N for a 5-second settle before
    re-applying). The three-repeat means are averaged to produce a single
    (raw, F) point for the fit.

3.5 Settle between levels: the MTS transitions to the next force level at
    0.5 N/s ramp rate. After the ramp, a 5-second dwell is required before
    the settle timer (item 3.2) starts.

3.6 Sensor conditioning: before calibration data collection, each sensor
    receives three full-range load-unload cycles (0 N to FS, 30 seconds
    hold, unload at 0.5 N/s). This is a manufacturer-recommended warm-up
    that reduces creep hysteresis in the first acquisition.

3.7 DAQ state: the DAQ is streaming at 100 Hz (host command 0x64 per Data
    Stream Format). Timestamps are recorded in each sample frame header.
    The calibration acquisition script reads from /dev/ttyUSB0 via

    c. Adjusted R-squared of the log-log linear regression >= 0.998

This Bill enacts the following seven-part calibration protocol. Enactment
means the protocol becomes the standing procedure for all subsequent per-channel
fits. Nothing in the protocol takes effect until the Justice enacts this Bill.

---- PART 1: Curve Form ----

FlexiForce sensors operate by piezoresistive conductance: applied force reduces
resistance approximately as F ~ 1/(R - R0), which yields a sub-linear
(concave-down) mapping from raw ADC code to force when the ADC measures voltage
across a fixed feedback resistor. Over the narrow operating ranges of this
project the response is well-described by a two-parameter power law of the form:

    F(raw) = a * raw^b

where a > 0 and b > 0. This form:
(a) captures the compressive stiffening of the sensor's elastomeric layer at
    higher loads without introducing an offset parameter that would require a
    third calibration point to constrain;
(b) passes through F = 0 at raw = 0, which is the correct quiescent state
    (zero applied force, zero ADC output) — a linear form F = a*raw + b
    introduces a non-physical offset and requires the operator to manually
    enforce F(0) = 0 by constraining b = 0, collapsing it to F = a*raw
    (which is too rigid for the known non-linearity);
(c) is identifiable with as few as 5 well-distributed calibration points and
    is numerically stable when fit in log-log space (log F = log a + b * log raw)
    using ordinary least squares.

Different curve forms for the two sensor families are not proposed: the power
law is appropriate for both, with different fitted coefficients (a, b) reflecting
the different full-scale ranges. A two-segment piecewise linear form would require
explicit knee-point identification, which adds operator judgement; an exponential
form (F = a*exp(b*raw) + c) adds a third parameter that is underdetermined at
five points. The power law is the minimum-parameter form consistent with the
physics.

The per-channel fit is:
    F_ch[N]  (N) = a_ch * (raw_ch)^b_ch

where a_ch and b_ch are the two fitted scalars unique to each channel.

family show consistent order-of-magnitude response but differ in actual
conductance by up to ±30% across production units (per vendor characterisation

verification would systematically mis-calibrate the minority of channels that
fall in the tails of the production distribution. Pooling is inadmissible unless,
after all seven individual fits are complete, the maximum pairwise residual
difference across same-family channels is less than 2% of the family full-scale
(< 0.088 N for A301-1, < 2.2 N for A301-25). This pre-condition is not expected
to be met and is included only to document the criterion by which pooling could
ever be reconsidered at a future Hearing.

applies a known quasi-static compressive force to the sensor surface with sub-

3.1 Force levels per channel:

        0.25 N, 0.44 N, 0.77 N, 1.35 N, 1.76 N, 2.64 N, 3.52 N, 4.18 N

    - A301-25 channels (Ch5–Ch6, full-scale 110 N): 8 levels:
        6.6 N, 11 N, 19 N, 33 N, 55 N, 77 N, 99 N, 110 N

      full-scale as an upper anchor).

    Rationale for log spacing: the power-law form is fit in log-log space;
    log spacing produces equal density of points per decade, minimising the
    condition number of the log-log regression. Eight points provides three
    degrees of freedom above the two-parameter fit and is sufficient to detect
    a systematic third-order deviation.

    ADC circuit and the uncertainty in raw is large relative to the signal.

content.text:
Good question — and the right time to ask it, because if drift handling is missing from both Bills, neither is closure-ready.

## What FlexiForce drift actually looks like

A301 has three drift modes, in decreasing severity for this benchmark:

1. **Sustained-load creep** — held at constant force, the sensor reads *progressively higher* over time. Tekscan characterizes it as roughly `~5% per decade of log(time)` of applied load. Most creep happens in the first ~10 s of loading; it flattens out logarithmically after that.
2. **Hysteresis** — same applied force reads differently on the up-cycle vs down-cycle, typically 4–5% of full-scale.
3. **Long-term zero drift** — amplifier offset and sensor quiescent conductance shift over hours-to-days.

## What this means for *your* metrics

- **Metric #4 (peak grasp force)** — captured at the *moment of pinch*. Sensor has just gone unloaded → loaded; creep hasn't started. Good signal, drift-immune within trial.
- **Metric #5 (min force for grasp)** — same: it's the threshold crossing, a *transition* event. Drift-immune.
- **Metric #3 (max admissible surface force)** — this one is *sustained* table-contact during pre-pinch descent. Creep makes the sensor read **higher than truth** by potentially several percent within a trial. This biases the controller-quit threshold to fire earlier than the true force boundary, and the bias differs depending on how long a given trial sits in pre-pinch contact.
- **Bench-foot A301-1 array** — sensors are *always* under static bench weight. The absolute reading is contaminated by long-term drift; the *change* during a trial is not. Use differential measurement (baseline subtraction) for all bench-foot metrics.

## The benchmark's saving grace

This is a **comparison**, not an absolute measurement. If both soft and rigid graspers experience the same creep on the same hardware, the bias **partially cancels in the comparison envelope**. The danger is *trial-order coupling*: if you run all-soft then all-rigid, accumulated creep across the session shifts the rigid-grasper measurements. Randomized interleaved trial order breaks that confound for free.

## Concrete mitigations (in order of cost vs benefit)

| Mitigation | Cost | What it buys |
|---|---|---|
| Randomized interleaved soft/rigid trial order | Zero | Cancels session-level drift in the comparison |
| Per-trial baseline subtraction (use Δforce, not absolute) | Trivial — post-processing | Cancels slow zero drift on all metrics that are "change during trial" |
| Cap sustained pre-pinch dwell time at a fixed budget (e.g., ≤ 3 s) | Low — controller config | Bounds creep contribution to metric #3 by capping its time-domain integral |
| Re-zero between trials (3 s no-contact window) | Already in Calibration Bill (5.3) | Catches slow drift mid-session |
| MTS step-response characterization — apply step load, sample at 100 Hz for 30 s, fit creep coefficient per channel | Medium — adds ~10 min per channel to calibration | Lets you *correct* sustained readings post-hoc; needed only if metric #3 turns out to be the dominant comparison dimension |
| Load-unload hysteresis sweep on MTS | Medium — adds ~10 min per channel | Bounds hysteresis error; mostly cosmetic for this benchmark since pinch is one-directional |

The first four are essentially free and you should adopt them. Step-response characterization is the only one where I'd actually deliberate — it's "deep instrumentation" rigor that may pay off if metric #3 ends up being the discriminating axis, and may not if the soft-vs-rigid difference shows up first in metrics #1, #2, or #4/#5.

## How to fold this into the hearing

Three reasonable paths:

content.text:
Two clarifications, in order.

## 1. What is Position B?

In a Crucible Judicial Hearing, the Justice (you) declares two opposing positions and assigns one to each attorney. The attorneys argue them physically and constitutionally; you rule.

- **Position A** is "enact the Bill as drafted." It's the default proposal.
- **Position B** is whatever the *strongest credible challenge* to Position A is. It doesn't have to be a position you believe — it has to be the position that, if Position A can survive arguing against it, makes the ratification load-bearing. If Position B is a strawman, the hearing is theatre.

You pick Position B because *you* are the Justice — you decide which dimension of the proposal you most want stress-tested. The three options I gave earlier were three different "where might this Bill be wrong" framings: form choice, ordering, or rigor level.

You can also just say "I don't think there's a meaningful counter — skip the hearing and enact by precedent." That's a legitimate Justice move; you'd record the lack of debate in case_law.md as the reasoning.

## 2. What you actually do when calibrating

Here is the protocol the Calibration Bill encodes, in plain language, with the *why* attached. This is what physically happens during one MTS calibration session for one channel:

**Setup (once per channel, before any data):**
1. Mount the sensor in the MTS with the load applicator aligned to the sensitive area.
2. Verify DAQ is streaming the channel at 100 Hz, frames syncing on `0xAA`/`0x55`.
3. **Warm-up:** run 3 full load-unload cycles up to full-scale, holding at FS for 30 s each, unloading at 0.5 N/s. *Why: a fresh A301 has a "first-loading" transient that biases the first calibration point downward by a few percent. After 3 cycles the response stabilizes.*

**At each of the 8 force levels (ascending: low → high):**
1. Command MTS to ramp to the target force at 0.5 N/s.
2. Once at force, **wait 5 seconds settled**. *Why: this lets the fast creep transient finish — most creep happens in the first few seconds; sampling after that gives you the "stable" reading.*
3. Sample the DAQ for **1 second (= 100 samples at 100 Hz)**. Record:
   - `raw_mean` (the calibration point)
   - `raw_std` (the noise on that point — if > 15 ADC counts, discard and re-acquire)
   - the MTS-applied force in N
4. **Unload back to 0 N**, wait 5 seconds for the sensor to recover.
5. Repeat steps 1–4 **3 times** for this force level. Average the three `raw_mean` values → final point.
6. Move to next force level.

**Force levels for A301-1 (0–4.4 N range):** 0.25, 0.44, 0.77, 1.35, 1.76, 2.64, 3.52, 4.18 N.
**Force levels for A301-25 (0–110 N range):** 6.6, 11, 19, 33, 55, 77, 99, 110 N.

*Why log-spaced: you're fitting `F = a·raw^b` in log-log space — equally spaced log-points give the regression equal information per decade.*

**After all 8 levels collected:**
1. Fit `log(F) = log(a) + b · log(raw)` by ordinary least squares.
2. Compute residuals in *Newtons* (not log space — convert back).
3. Check acceptance: RMS residual ≤ 2% FS, max residual ≤ 4% FS, R² of the log-log fit ≥ 0.998.
4. If accepted: write `docs/calibration/ch<N>_<date>.json` with the coefficients and the raw point set. Update `docs/toolchain_config.md`. The channel is now admissible.
5. If rejected: do *not* relax the criteria. Diagnose (sensor seated wrong? cable wiggle? amplifier saturating at the top end?) and re-acquire that channel.

**Total time per channel:** ~25 minutes (3 warm-up cycles × 3 min + 8 levels × 3 repeats × ~30 s each, plus settle).
**For all 7 channels:** ~3 hours of MTS bench time.

## What the protocol does NOT cover (the drift question)

The above gets you a static `F(raw)` mapping accurate at the moment of stable load. It does **not** correct for:

- **Creep during sustained load in a real trial** — if your trial holds table contact for 5 s, the sensor reads higher than truth by a small percentage that grows logarithmically with time.
- **Hysteresis** — same applied force reads different on the way up vs the way down.
- **Inter-session zero drift** — caught by the session-start zero-load check; the protocol handles this.

For the cloth-grasp benchmark, those three modes affect different metrics differently. **The peak grasp force (metric #4) and minimum grasp force (metric #5) are essentially drift-immune** — they're transition events captured before creep starts. **The sustained surface force (metric #3) is the one creep contaminates** — and there, the cheap mitigations (cap pre-pinch dwell, use baseline-subtracted Δforce, randomize trial order between graspers) get you most of the way without needing a separate step-response calibration.

So the practical answer is: **run the protocol above as written, and choose separately whether you also want a 5-minute-per-channel step-response calibration on the MTS to enable drift correction for metric #3 specifically.** That step-response addendum is what the three Position B options I offered were poking at from different angles.

- **Physical / clinical outcome protected** — what physically goes right if this position prevails.
- **Consequences of opposing position in physical terms** — what physically goes wrong if Position B prevails.

content.text:
Your instinct is right, and it's a stronger Position B than anything I offered. Let me explain why, then propose it formally.

## Why early-window averaging is *better* than the Bill's 5 s settle

A301 creep is **monotonic and logarithmic**: held at a constant true force, the reading drifts *upward* over time. So:

- At t = 0.5 s post-load: reading is ~`F_true × (1 + ε_0.5)` — small creep error.
- At t = 5 s post-load: reading is ~`F_true × (1 + ε_5)` with `ε_5 > ε_0.5` — larger creep error.
- At t = 30 s: larger still.

The current Bill samples at 5+ seconds (waits for "settling"). But the sensor never *settles* in the creep sense — it just creeps more slowly. So the 5 s reading is **further from true applied force** than a 1 s reading.

**Average of 0.5–2.5 s post-load**:
- Skips mechanical transients (load-cell ringing, elastomer-contact dynamics) in the first ~300 ms.
- Captures the reading while cumulative creep is still small (logarithmic creep is mostly accumulated after the first decade of time; at 2 s post-load you're only ~1% above the t=0 ideal).
- Averaging over 2 s of 100 Hz samples = 200 samples → noise floor is fine.

## The deeper reason this is better

**Match the calibration timescale to the trial timescale.** In a real grasp trial, force on a bench foot is applied for ~1–3 seconds before the pinch event resolves. Finger-pad pinch peak is sub-second. So:

- Calibrate at 5 s settled, measure trial at 1.5 s → systematic mismatch ≈ creep between 1.5 s and 5 s (a few percent).
- Calibrate at 0.5–2.5 s mean, measure trial at 1.5 s → calibration and trial sit in the *same creep regime*; the creep error mostly cancels.

This is the same principle as "always calibrate the way you measure." The 5 s settled protocol assumes the sensor reaches a stable state — for an A301, that's never true.

## What it costs

| Item | Current Bill | Your proposal |
|---|---|---|
| Per-level acquisition | 5 s settle + 1 s sample + 5 s recovery × 3 repeats = ~33 s | 2.5 s sample + 3 s recovery × maybe 2 repeats = ~11 s |
| Required MTS ramp rate | 0.5 N/s (slow — reaches 4.4 N in 8.8 s, 110 N in 220 s) | Fast enough to reach target in <0.5 s — for A301-1 that's ≥10 N/s; for A301-25 that's ≥200 N/s |
| Per-channel time | ~25 min | ~5–8 min |
| Total for 7 channels | ~3 hours | ~45 min |

**One check before this becomes Position B**: does your MTS support fast force-control ramps? Most MTS frames do (modern servohydraulic or electromechanical units ramp at hundreds of N/s easily), but some older or displacement-control-only units can't. If yours can ramp to 110 N in <0.5 s, this works as-is. If not, you'd need to fall back to a step-and-hold protocol where the MTS pre-loads and then a release mechanism applies the step.

## Position B, formalized

> **Position B: "The Calibration Bill's 5-second settle + 1-second sample window is the wrong timescale. A301 creep is logarithmic, not relaxational — the 'settled' reading is further from true applied force than an early-window reading. The protocol should be replaced with: rapid MTS ramp to target (<0.5 s), then 2-second average of samples over the 0.5–2.5 s post-load window, matching the trial's actual force-application timescale. This reduces per-channel time by ~4× and reduces systematic creep bias in the fitted curve."**

The amendment grounding for Position B is **Amendment 1 (Domain Primitives)** — specifically, the Contact Force primitive must be calibrated against the measurement *the trial actually performs*; calibrating at a timescale the trial never sees introduces a hidden systematic that biases the comparison.

Yes — absolutely. I should have stated that explicitly. Let me clarify.

## What Position B *changes* vs what it *keeps*

**Position B keeps everything about the curve-fitting structure:**
- 8 log-spaced force levels per channel (same as Bill: 0.25 → 4.18 N for A301-1; 6.6 → 110 N for A301-25)
- Per-channel power-law fit `F = a·raw^b` in log-log space
- Same acceptance criteria (RMS ≤ 2% FS, max ≤ 4% FS, R² ≥ 0.998)
- Same warm-up (3 full load-unload cycles before data)
- Same per-channel JSON storage and admissibility binding
- 3 repeats per level (or some defensible number — see below)

**Position B *only* changes the per-level timing window** — i.e., *how* a single (raw, applied_force) calibration point is acquired:

| Step | Bill (Position A) | Position B |
|---|---|---|
| Ramp to target force | 0.5 N/s | rapid (<0.5 s to target) |
| Settle wait before sampling | 5 s | ~0.3 s (skip mechanical transient only) |
| Sample window | 1 s @ 100 Hz = 100 samples, starting at t = 5 s post-load | 2 s @ 100 Hz = 200 samples, starting at t = 0.5 s post-load (window 0.5–2.5 s) |
| Recovery between repeats | 5 s unloaded | 3–5 s unloaded |
| Repeats per level | 3 | 3 (could argue 2 — but keep 3 for symmetry with A) |

The fit itself is identical — 8 (raw_mean, F_applied) points → log-log OLS → coefficients (a, b). Position B only argues that each (raw_mean, F_applied) point should come from an early-window measurement, not a late-window one.

## Re-worded Position B

> **Position B: "The Calibration Bill's per-level acquisition timing (5 s settle + 1 s sample) is the wrong timescale for the A301's logarithmic creep behavior. The 8-level log-spaced sweep, per-channel power-law fit, 3 repeats, acceptance criteria, JSON storage, and admissibility binding are all retained as drafted. Only the per-level sampling window changes: rapid MTS ramp to target (<0.5 s), then average DAQ samples over the 0.5–2.5 s post-load window (200 samples at 100 Hz). Rationale: A301 creep is monotonic and logarithmic — the 'settled' reading at t = 5 s is further from the true applied force than an early-window reading, and the trial measurement timescale (~1–3 s of applied force per trial) is the one calibration should match. This reduces per-channel acquisition time by ~3–4× and removes a systematic creep bias from the fitted curve."**

- **Add the Amendment 1 grounding sentence** as part of the formal position rather than separate.
- **Specify whether the 200-sample average is a mean, median, or trimmed mean** — early-window data may have residual ramp-end ringing that median handles better than mean.
